title: Concrete timed simulation bound
statement: For every effective machine coding scheme $c$, there is a finite-tape machine $U$ over the Boolean alphabet such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$, Boolean input $x$, and natural number $t$, both of the following hold. Write $L$ for the length of the canonical serialization of the machine decoded from $\alpha$, $N$ for its state-count parameter, $q$ for its initial-state index, and $T(n)$ for the canonizer's time bound. If the decoded machine computes output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes $1$ followed by $y$ on $\langle\langle\operatorname{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly $C_{c,\alpha}(t+1)^2$ steps; if it computes no output on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes the one-bit output $0$ on that input in exactly the same number of steps, where $C_{c,\alpha}=(3|\alpha|+T(|\alpha|)+L+2|\operatorname{bin}(N)|+2q+16)+(3L+5(N+1)+20)+14$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective machine coding scheme
replaced:
For every effective machine-coding scheme $c$, there is a single finite-tape machine $U$
over $\{0,1\}$ such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$, input $x$, and deadline
$t\in\mathbb{N}$, the following hold. Write $L$ for the length of the canonical
serialization of the machine decoded from $\alpha$, $N$ for its number of states, $q$
for the index of its initial state, and $T(n)$ for the running-time bound of the
scheme's canonizer. If the decoded machine computes output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$
steps, then $U$ computes $1$ followed by $y$ on
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly $C_\alpha(t+1)^2$
steps; if it computes no output on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes the
one-bit output $0$ on that input in exactly the same number of steps, where
$C_\alpha=(3|\alpha|+T(|\alpha|)+L+2|\mathrm{bin}(N)|+2q+16)+(3L+5(N+1)+20)+14$.
